'''Gold Enemies''', also known as '''Golden Monsters''', are recurring [[Enemy|Enemies]] in {{TLoZ Series}}. They are much more difficult to defeat than their regular counterparts, with improved speed, power or health. In return, the reward for defeating these rare [[Monster]]s is substantially higher. Their appearance is usually tied to the activation of an event, such as a [[Kinstone Fusion]] in {{TMC}}.<ref>{{Cite|Have you ever seen a golden monster? When you fuse Kinstone pieces, you might get the rare chance to meet one.|Swordsman Newsletter 4|TMC}}</ref>

==Characteristics==
==={{OoS|-}}===
[[File:OoS Golden Sage Sprite.png|left|32px|The [[Golden Sage]]]]
In [[Summer]], the [[Water (Terrain)|Water]] around [[Gnarled Root Dungeon]] recedes, revealing a cave with the [[Golden Sage]] inside. After [[Link]] talks to him, four different Golden Monsters will appear around various regions of [[Holodrum]]. When all four have been defeated, Link can return to the Golden Sage to receive a [[Magic Ring]] which, when appraised by [[Vasu]], becomes the powerful [[Red Ring]].<ref>{{Cite Guide|OoS Nintendo|page= 17}}</ref>

==={{TMC|-}}===
Three types of Golden Monsters appear across [[Hyrule]] after certain [[Kinstone Fusion]]s in {{TMC}}. They are [[Octorok]]s, [[Tektite]]s, and [[Rope]]s. After one is defeated, they will drop a large sum of [[Rupee]]s.

==={{BotW|-}}===
In [[Master Mode]] in {{BotW}}, [[Golden Bokoblin]]s, [[Golden Moblin]]s, [[Golden Lizalfos]], and [[Golden Lynel]]s appear as a stronger variant than silver [[Enemy|Enemies]]. Unlike the other variants, Golden Monsters have a stronger resistance to status effects, such as Shock, [[Ice]], and [[Fire]]. They can recover from being shocked faster, thaw out of Ice faster, and are not as susceptible to Flames.
